steps.title: Begin with two separate unloaded blocks
steps.explanation: The second reference cross-section is twice the first. A massless spacer transmits the same axial force and allows the blocks to slide laterally at their ideal fixtures.
steps.observe: Both stretches and measured volume ratios are 1; current areas are 300 and 600 mm². The gap and grey connector represent the spacer, not missing tissue.

steps.title: Transmit one tensile force
steps.explanation: Apply +0.1 N to both blocks. The narrower block needs twice the nominal stress, so the same neo-Hookean law gives it the greater stretch.
steps.observe: Stretches are about 1.07983 and 1.03844; current areas shrink to 277.821 and 577.788 mm². Each measured volume ratio remains 1.

steps.title: Reverse the signed load
steps.explanation: Apply −0.1 N using the same bilateral fixtures. The narrower block now shortens more and expands more laterally; neither block changes its local volume.
steps.observe: Stretches become about 0.931143 and 0.964301; areas become 322.185 and 622.212 mm². The shared force does not imply equal stress or equal strain.

steps.title: Expose finite root error
steps.explanation: Restore tension but reduce the bisection cap to eight. Incompressibility remains imposed exactly while axial force balance is only approximated.
steps.observe: The maximum force residual is about 0.00164715 N, above the 1e-10 N criterion, so Converged is false even though both volumes are preserved.

audit.finding: Current areas and force residuals were absent, and the spacer had no visual explanation.
audit.change: Display the ideal connector, measured areas and actual force criterion; compare unloaded, tensile, compressive and unconverged cases.
audit.remaining: Separate homogeneous incompressible blocks with ideal bilateral fixtures. No continuous taper, interface stress field, unrestricted stability or anatomical calibration.
